## LLM Recipe

### 1.7 Reinforcement Learning &amp; Reasoning

#### [Training Small Language Models for Transferable Tool Selection](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31483>)

This recipe teaches a small model to decompose an instruction, retrieve candidate tools and select the needed set, using supervised warm-up followed by separate reinforcement-learning rewards for planning and selection. The trained policy transfers to different tool corpora and a replacement retriever without retraining, suggesting a way to specialize the tool-selection step while keeping each model call small.

**Published:** 2026-10-22 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:02:54.787Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Tool Selection, Reinforcement Learning, Domain Transfer

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.31483v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 full primary HTML and 19-page PDF retrieved; Sections3–4, Tables1–4, ablations, AppendixA training/evaluation, AppendixB artifact identities, AppendixC release status and AppendixD prompts inspected. One Qwen3 model serves a stateless planner and selector; BM25 retrieves at most15 candidates per substep, and the selector commits one tool. The training pipeline filters ambiguous/redundant ToolBench gold labels with a Llama-4-Maverick teacher, then creates20,093 curated training instructions and teacher-written Plan/Select reasoning trajectories. GRPO trains the two stages separately: planning receives an F1-like reward combining unique gold coverage and reciprocal-rank-weighted recall, while selection receives exact-match reward on teacher-written substeps. Thus the selector is trained on teacher plans rather than jointly optimizing full student-generated trajectories. All parameters are trained: three SFT epochs, then300 GRPO steps at64 prompts and16 rollouts per prompt on8A100 GPUs, shared across1.7B/4B/8B models. On2,124 filtered ToolBenchG3 test instructions, exact tool-set success rises from36.2% afterSFT to41.5% afterSFT+RL for8B; the strongest prompted Maverick protocol reports30.6%, with its own interaction budgets. Transfer uses the same G3-trained checkpoints:8B reports25.8% G2,29.9% Gorilla,69.0% CRAFT and72.8% TaskBench; Maverick Search-R1-style scores80.6% onTaskBench, so there is no universal win. Swapping BM25 for a trained COLT retriever uses the same policy/prompts, with the retrieval-score threshold adjusted from3 to0.6. Original submissionOctober22T16:07:49UTC retained; the original FridayOctober23 cs.LG dated batch and official Eastern-time schedule imply paper announcementOctober23T00:00UTC, within theOctober24 report72-hour lookback. The title was encountered in theOctober23 primary-index screening and left unselected; full methods/evidence review was completed during this delayedOctober25 execution for the missingOctober24 report. Its earlier actual indexed first-seen is retained. No indexing-delay explanation is asserted. Bounded exact-title/author-artifact searches did not establish an earlier matching release. AppendixC explicitly states that the derived data, trained checkpoints and author training/evaluation code are not released, so background framework links are not presented as this work's code.

**Limitations:** This evaluates selection of tool IDs, not executing tools or completing consequential agent tasks. The workflow assumes independent substeps that each require one tool, limiting dependent multi-turn workflows. Gold-label filtering changes both training and the G2/G3 evaluation target; success is against these curated sets. Prompted baselines and trained models differ in interaction budgets, native-thinking settings and specialized training, so the comparison is not a matched-compute claim that8B generally exceeds402B. Each reported result is one evaluation run without a multi-training-seed study; batched inference itself can change one or two instruction outcomes. The strongest TaskBench comparison favors Maverick. No author-derived data, checkpoints or implementation are released, and no independent reproduction or end-to-end cost/latency benefit is verified.

### 1.10 Model Evaluation, Safety &amp; Interpretability

#### [Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31639>)

CausalCoT plans a graph of subquestions and evaluates its nodes in separate contexts, passing explicit parent findings onward instead of letting every step reread the whole question. This makes final answers more responsive to targeted edits of intermediate reasoning in the tested tasks, offering an auditable inference workflow with an accuracy and computation trade-off rather than a guarantee about a model's internal reasoning.

**Published:** 2026-10-22 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:02:55.475Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Reasoning Faithfulness, Context Isolation, Test-time Interventions

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.31639v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Pinned v1 full primary HTML and38-page PDF retrieved; main Sections3–5/7 and Tables1–2, formal-scoping AppendixD, experimental/implementation AppendicesF–G, relevant isolation/variability/evaluator/failure/cost analyses H.5–H.11 and prompt interfaces inspected. A model first proposes a directed acyclic graph; roots receive the original question, while descendant calls receive their local subquestion and direct-parent question/FINDING summaries. The final node does not concatenate the full question and global trace. An implementation fallback can reclassify an insufficient-context internal node as a root and then give it the original question; this is not an immutable no-global-input guarantee at every originally internal node. The paper specifies200 sampled items each fromMedQA,GPQA andCounterfactuals, with three independently regenerated plans/generations per item, seven model variants spanning Gemma3,GPT-5.4 andClaude4.5/4.6, and CoT/factored-decomposition baselines. GPT-5.4 provides step edits, predicted implications and simulated expert corrections. Table2 GPT-5.4 average answer-change rate is48.43% versus27.24% for factored decomposition and26.82% forCoT, while predictable-change is70.52% versus57.60%/54.27%. Table1 its average unedited accuracy is72.18%, belowCoT74.36%; sensitivity is not itself correctness. Reusing stored DAGs in NoTrim controls helps separate isolation from decomposition: onGPT-5.4Mini, aggregate answer-change drops from58.72 to37.07 when original context is reintroduced (a separate stored-DAG analysis, not the main table value). AppendixH.8 finds only roughly73–82% of sampled automatic step edits valid across raters, despite higher expected-label validity. The50-itemMedQA/GPT-5.4Mini overhead check reports237 generation calls and3.43minutes forCausalCoT versus50calls/1.31minutes forCoT, without establishing deployment-wide latency. Original receiptOctober22T17:52:56UTC retained; originalFridayOctober23 cs.LG batch plus official schedule supports inferred paper announcementOctober23T00:00UTC. This was an abstract/full-text-access reserve first encounteredOctober23 and not selected then; its full method/result review is completed now as a deliberate missingOctober24-window catch-up. The first-seen timestamp is preserved; no indexing delay is claimed. No earlier matching author release was verified in bounded exact-title searches; similarly named older Causal-CoT papers are different methods. Author code is described as a future release, with no actual author implementation URL verified.

**Limitations:** Causal means procedural input routing, not structural-causal identification, mechanistic faithfulness, accurate real-world reasoning or guaranteed safe decisions. Parametric knowledge, information encoded by the planner and bad/missing dependencies remain; roots see the original input and fallback changes the graph. Empirical faithfulness relies on model-generated perturbations and judges with imperfect edit validity, and the displayed standard errors mostly summarize three generation resamples rather than dataset or training-seed uncertainty. Stronger compliance with a wrong intermediate premise can reduce accuracy rather than improve reasoning. Main evidence is multiple-choice QA; open-ended use is discussed but not experimentally established. Simulated GPT corrections are not a human intervention trial. Runtime figures come from50MedQA items with provider-dependent API concurrency, not matched hardware throughput; the method costs more thanCoT in that check. No verified author code release or independent reproduction.

### 2.7 Agent Harness &amp; Reliability

#### [From Prose to Properties: Testing Research Claims with ARATest for Agent-Native Science](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30495>)

ARATest turns explicitly scoped research claims into typed property checks that reuse fixed decision rules across reported tables and agent-run experiments, retaining replayable counterexamples. The new evaluation of the existing library shows that deterministic checking can catch numerical contradictions that language-model judges miss, while leaving ambiguous or insufficiently supported claims undecided.

### 3.6 Low-Precision &amp; Efficient Execution

#### [vLLM Delivers Day-0 Support for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-minimax-m31-flash>)

vLLM adapts MiniMax-M3.1-Flash’s native four-bit cache and expert weights to NVIDIA and AMD GPUs using fused dequantization, sparse-attention kernels and context-parallel indexing. The report shows how low-precision storage must be paired with hardware-specific data movement and execution changes to turn smaller tensors into useful serving gains, and provides checkpoints, kernels and deployment recipes.

**Published:** 2026-10-23 · **First seen:** 2026-10-23T10:03:45.102Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** NVFP4, Sparse Attention, GPU Kernels, Serving Recipes

[Blog](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-23-minimax-m31-flash>) · [Code](<https://github.com/vllm-project/MSA>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Delayed editorial catch-up of the October 23 report; its title was observed October 23, then fully reviewed today. Older MSA kernels predate this report. Native NVFP4 KV/expert storage is paired with fused dequantization, cache insertion and context-parallel indexing. Blackwell converts NVFP4 KV to FP8 for attention arithmetic. On GB300, QKV/norm/RoPE/cache-insert fusion reports 1.1–1.6× operator prefill speed and about 19% lower P50 time to first token at TP4. AgentX throughput counts cached input, uncached input and output, with synthetic speculative acceptance.

**Limitations:** Kernel and end-to-end gains are separate; cross-checkpoint cache capacity is not an equal-quality ablation. Hardware/workloads vary across NVIDIA/AMD. Vendor containers precede upstream/nightly-wheel merging. Neither independent reproduction nor universal quality preservation is established.
